text.p: Hechinger Co, Kmart Corp and Leonard Green & Partners LP said Thursday they had a definitive pact to create the nation's third largest home improvement chain by uniting Hechinger with Kmart's Builders Square.

Holders of Hechinger Class A and Class B shares will receive $3 cash per share under the deal, which Hechinger said represents a 100 percent premium over the Class A price the week before the announcement of a possible transaction.
The combination unites 162 Builders Square stores in the Midwest and Southwest with Hechinger's 117 home improvement stores in the Midwest and on the East Coast.
The combined entity will have 279 stores in 29 states and the District of Columbia and have combined annual revenues of more than $4.5 billion, the group said.
Leonard Green & Partners will own 100 percent of the new company through an investment partnership. Kmart will receive a warrant to purchase a minority interest at a later date, the group said.

The group said Anthony Petrillo will serve as acting chief executive of the new company. Petrillo has more than 35 years of experience in retail and has worked with Leonard Green & Partners in its retailing portfolio companies since 1994.

Leonard Green said it has provided the new company with financial flexibility to commit significant capital to refurbish, remodel and remerchandise its stores to improve customer service and revitalize its business.
"We believe the combination provides major opportunities for expense savings, marketing synergies and improved purchasing power," said Jonathan Sokoloff, a partner at Leonard Green & Partners.
Financing is being arranged by Chase Manhattan Corp in conjunction with BankAmerica Business Credit Inc and Citicorp USA Inc, a subsidiary of Citibank.
The deal is subject to customary regulatory approvals, bank financing and approval by Hechinger shareholders.
Hechinger Class A shares closed Thursday down 1/8 at 2. Its class B shares closed unchanged at 3, and those of Kmart closed unchanged at 10-3/4.
